title: Bound for an integrated Gaussian density Hessian
statement:
Let $I$ be a finite index set, and let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f(z)|\leq1$ for every $z$. Let $v\geq0$ with $v\ne0$, and let $c\in\mathbb R^I$. The norm of the integral of $f(z)$ times the product Gaussian density Hessian with mean $c$ and variance $v$, integrated against Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^I$, is at most
\[
|I|^2\frac{2}{v}.
\]
replaced: Let $I$ be finite and $v\ge0$. Put $G_v(c,z)=\prod_i p_v(c_i,z_i)$, where $p_v$ is the Gaussian density of variance $v$ for $v>0$ and $p_0=0$, and put $S_v(c,z)[h]=\sum_i((z_i-c_i)/v)h_i$, with division by zero equal to zero. Define $A_v(c,z)[h]=G_v(c,z)S_v(c,z)[h]$ and $T_v(c,z)[h,k]=G_v(c,z)(S_v(c,z)[h]S_v(c,z)[k]-\sum_i h_i k_i/v)$. Let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f|\le1$. If $v>0$, then $\|\int f(z)T_v(c,z)\,dz\|\le2|I|^2/v$ for every $c\in\mathbb R^I$, using maximum norms for the bilinear operator norm.
